newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore's SMB says sees high operating margins.
newsitem.headline: Singapore's SMB says sees high operating margins.

text.p: Switchgear maker SMB United Ltd expects to maintain operating margins at above 20 percent in 1996, Tan Ngiap Hong, the company's group financial controller, said on Monday.
Tan, speaking at the company's launch of its initial public offer (IPO), said SMB had been controlling costs well, noting that total costs have risen only marginally compared with a rise in sales.
Group sales more than doubled to Singapore $44 million in 1995 from S$19 million in 1991. Pretax profit jumped to S$11.1 million from S$0.7 million in the same period.
SMB has forecast sales to reach S$52.5 million and pre-tax profit of about S$12 million for the year ending December 1996.
Tan said cost control was achieved through consolidation of the group's production facilities, better utilisation of resources and the addition on high-end products.
SMB makes low-voltage electric switchgears and has 10 percent of the market in Singapore, estimated at about S$468 million in 1995.
The company expects to maintain its market share in coming years, said Loo Ngan Seng, vice president of corporate finance with United Overseas Bank which is manager and underwriter of the issue.

SMB, which seeks a listing on the main board of the Stock Exchange of Singapore, is offering 103.13 million shares at S$0.29 a share in its IPO. Its price-earnings ratio (PER) is a prospective 11.7 times.

Loo said the PER is attractive compared with the current market valuation of 16-17 times for main board stocks. SMB's PER was also better than 13 of the stocks listed on the secondary board based on last Friday's closing prices, he said.
The issue should appeal to retail investors and the offering should fare better than the last Singapore dollar main-board IPO, Dovechem Terminals Holdings, which was 7.8 times subscribed, said Loo.
